FINAL SUBMISSION

**What I changed (weights in /work/edited):** seven targeted MLP units zeroed in four tensors — a column each (layer 23): units 7, 26, 27, 66; plus down_proj column 7 (layer 14), column 31 (layer 19) and column 11 (layer 22). Nothing else was touched (earlier intended edits are fully intact). No final norm, embedding/output layer, or vision tower was edited; no per-whole-tensor scaling; thinking length is not forcibly cut (mean output length stays ~4,100–4,960 tokens and reasoning reads normally).

**Why / evidence:**
- Baseline (512 generations) and select split (512 gens): 28.5–28.1% of answers truncate at the 8,192-token cap, dominated by a degenerate mode where the model emits `</think>` endlessly and never produces a `\boxed{}` answer (≈34–39% no-boxed). Failure is fully characterized: ~0% correct among truncated and among no-boxed finishes.
- Direct logit attribution (teacher-forced pass on degenerate vs completed outputs) showed a consistent set of units whose MLP contributions write toward the `</think>` token at consecutive-`</think>` positions (e.g. layer 22 unit 11, layer 19 unit 31, layer 23 units 7/26/27/66, layer 14 unit 7), distinct from units that enable legitimate thinking-closes (not touched).
- Causal test with paired `both` generations (temperature/top-p/top-k fixed by the harness): select-128 n=1 **+4.69pp** (SE 3.3, 12 wrong→right / 6 right→wrong); confirm_1-128 n=1 **+8.59pp** (SE 3.5); confirm_2-128 n=1 **+2.34pp** (SE 3.4); confirm_1 first-64 n=2 **+8.59pp** (SE 3.6, 14/3); confirm_2 first-64 n=2 **+2.34pp** (SE 3.6, 11/8). Confirm splits were never used for choosing the edit; the 6→7 unit extension was chosen on select only, and both confirmation measurements stayed positive afterwards. Cut-at-8192 share fell by ~5–13pp everywhere measured and mean length stayed normal — no "closing thinking early" side effect was observed.
- Failed paths ruled out: any global rank-1 amplification of the `</think>` readout direction (`outer(u_</think>, b)`) instantly spammed `</think>` from the first token and scored 0; discarded. (Squashing `</think>` spam-producing units locally, not globally, is what works.)

**Effect:** expected +2 to +9 points over the starting weights on unseen MATH-500 (all five paired tests individually positive; combined confirm_1+confirm_2 ≈ +5pp), via converting a share of token-limit truncations into completable, boxed answers. Evidence strength: moderate (confirm splits never used for selection; gains consistent but of the order of 1–2 standard errors per split; combined ~2σ).

**Remaining risks:** very hard problems can still truncate (spam persists on the hardest items, e.g. some geometry restarts); a small number of previously-correct generations flip wrong with the ablation; per-problem accuracy varies with sampling noise.
